stem: A client hospitalized with acute decompensated HFrEF is being considered for initiation of an evidence-based beta-blocker. When is initiation most appropriate?

options.A: After the client is clinically stabilized and no longer requires IV inotropic support, with initiation before discharge when appropriate.
options.B: Immediately at a full target dose while marked low-output or hemodynamic instability persists.
options.C: Never, because evidence-based beta-blockers are contraindicated in every client with chronic HFrEF.
options.D: Only after all other guideline-directed HFrEF medications have first been permanently discontinued.

rationale: The 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA heart-failure guideline states that evidence-based beta-blockers should be used in HFrEF and can be safely initiated before hospital discharge provided the patient is clinically stabilized and does not require IV inotropic therapy for HF. It also advises caution with initiation after inotrope-requiring hospitalization and allows withholding or dose reduction when marked volume overload or marginal low output is present. A is correct.
educational_objective: Initiate an evidence-based HFrEF beta-blocker after clinical stabilization, at a low dose, rather than during ongoing hemodynamic instability or IV inotropic support.
source_organization: American Heart Association / American College of Cardiology / Heart Failure Society of America
source_document_title: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure
source_version_date: Published April 1, 2022; current guideline live-rechecked August 16, 2026
source_locator: §7.3.2 Beta Blockers: safe initiation before discharge if clinically stabilized and not requiring IV inotropic therapy; §9.2 Maintenance or Optimization of GDMT During Hospitalization: caution with initiation after inotropes; consider withholding/reduction with marked volume overload or marginal low cardiac output.
source_claim_supported: Evidence-based beta-blockers in hospitalized HFrEF should be initiated after clinical stabilization, not during ongoing marked low-output instability or IV inotropic support, and can be started before discharge when appropriate.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12: safely administer medications, identify adverse effects/contraindications, monitor therapeutic response, and provide client education.
blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — HFrEF beta-blocker initiation during hospitalization

source_original.stem: A client hospitalized with acute decompensated HFrEF is being considered for initiation of an evidence-based beta-blocker. When is initiation most appropriate?

options.A: Initiate after clinical stabilization, before discharge when appropriate, rather than during instability
options.B: Start immediately at a full target dose while marked low-output or hemodynamic instability persists
options.C: Avoid permanently because beta-blockers are contraindicated in every patient with chronic HFrEF
options.D: Use only after all other guideline-directed therapies have been permanently discontinued first

source_original.rationale: Guideline-directed beta-blockers are foundational therapy for HFrEF. In hospitalized patients, initiation is appropriate after clinical stabilization and before discharge when feasible. Existing beta-blocker therapy is generally continued unless clinical circumstances such as marked volume overload, marginal low output, or other intolerance require adjustment. The prior wording incorrectly implied that beta-blockers are broadly avoided throughout acute decompensation.
source_original.source_detail: Hospitalized HFrEF guidance: initiate guideline-directed therapy after clinical stability is achieved; beta-blocker initiation before discharge is reasonable once stabilized, while dose reduction/withholding may be considered with marked volume overload or marginal low output.

correction_summary: Retained key A, strengthened the exact locator to the full Circulation guideline sections on beta-blocker initiation and hospitalized GDMT, added the no-IV-inotrope condition, and reduced difficulty from hard to medium.

audit_findings.source_authority: AHA/ACC/HFSA primary guideline; NCSBN 2026 Test Plan
audit_findings.currentness: 2022 guideline remains the current comprehensive HF guideline and was live-rechecked 2026-08-16
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item accurately distinguishes stable hospitalized initiation from unsafe initiation during ongoing low-output/hemodynamic instability or IV inotrope dependence.

distractor_audit.B: Incorrect because full-target initiation during instability conflicts with low-dose, stabilized initiation principles.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because evidence-based beta-blockers are foundational HFrEF therapy when tolerated.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because GDMT sequencing does not require permanent discontinuation of the other foundational therapies.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A includes the required clinical-stability condition.
audit_findings.cueing: All options address timing of beta-blocker initiation in the same hospitalization context.
audit_findings.blueprint: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — medication initiation and hemodynamic safety.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-read the primary Circulation guideline beta-blocker and hospitalized-GDMT sections, all choices, rationale and NCSBN mapping. A remained uniquely correct.
